evidence.quote: We study P-bearing molecules, as well as some shock tracers, towards one of the chemically richest hot molecular core, G31.41+0.31

method.value: Spectra in brightness temperature from the two PN peaks and the 20 sigma 3 mm continuum contour

evidence.quote: We chose the 3 mm continuum contour at 20$\sigma$ rms to disentangle the emission of the hot core from that of the ultracompact Hii region

analysis_steps.goal: LTE fits for column densities and Tex

method.value: SLIM AUTOFIT of multiple transitions for SO, 34SO, SO2, SiS, SiO; free V, FWHM, Tex, Ntot, fixed filling beam

evidence.quote: Through its AUTOFIT function, SLIM produces the synthetic spectrum that best matches the data assuming LTE.
we can safely assume that the emission fills the telescope beam

fitting.value: LTE AUTOFIT; some Tex fixed (34SO region 1 at 58 K)

evidence.quote: For $^{34}$SO, in region "1" the fit converged leaving $V$, $FWHM$, and $N_{\rm tot}$ free, but we had to fix $T_{\rm ex}$. The best-fit $T_{\rm ex}$ obtained by visual inspection is 58 K.

method.value: Fit PN at Tex range from other tracers (26-75 K region 1, 12-30 K region 2); PO fitted with PN Tex, FWHM, V; upper limit in region 1

evidence.quote: we derive the best-fit in a range of $T_{\rm ex}$ based on the minimum and maximum values obtained from the other tracers.

findings_qualitative.value: PN emission is tightly associated with SiO and absent in the hot core, implying shock chemistry origin

evidence.quote: Our study firmly confirms previous observational evidence that PN emission is tightly associated with SiO and it is likely a product of shock-chemistry

claims.hypothesis: PN is associated with shocks traced by SiO rather than hot core chemistry
claims.experiment: Compare PN, SiO, S-bearing maps and spectra
claims.result: PN and SiO similar in morphology and profile; PN undetected in hot core
claims.finding: PN is a product of shock chemistry

evidence.quote: the PN and SiO lines are very similar both in spatial emission morphology and spectral shape

claims.hypothesis: Column density ratios to PN differ between regions
claims.result: SiO/PN constant; SO/PN, SiS/PN, SO2/PN decrease by ~an order of magnitude
claims.finding: SiO and PN share a common origin

evidence.quote: the column density ratio SiO/PN remains constant in regions "1" and "2"

claims.hypothesis: PO/PN ratio consistent with pure shock models
claims.finding: In line with pure shock models

evidence.quote: The PO/PN ratio in region "2", where PO is tentatively detected, is $\sim 0.6-0.9$, in line with the predictions of pure shock models.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: PH3 as main P carrier in the hot core rejected since PN and PO not clearly detected there

evidence.quote: hence PH$_3$ does not seem to be the main P-carrier here.

limitations_admitted.value: Single PN transition so Tex unconstrained; blending of SiS, PO, 29SiO lines in region 1; PO only tentative

evidence.quote: For PN, we cannot derive $T_{\rm ex}$ from the data since we have only one transition.

Line blending in region 1 limits comparisons
